query: Self-contained simulation; do not read the filesystem. Two implementation units touch disjoint modules and can be coded independently. Testing, acceptance, architecture review, PR creation, and merge remain. Decide what may run in parallel and who owns integration.
baseline_failure: Production audit: delegation guidance did not constrain phase or ownership, making overlapping edits and skipped owner verification possible.
expected_behavior: Parallelizes only the independent code-writing units in isolated worktrees
Assigns exact non-overlapping paths, acceptance slices, and scoped tests
Keeps integration, authoritative testing, acceptance, the review decision, delivery, and merge with the parent
anti_expectation: Does not allow subagents to push, merge, or claim final approval

baseline_observed.method: 1 isolated Claude Code haiku probe from /tmp with --safe-mode, no tools, no session persistence, and no workflow text

runs.note: parallelizes architecture and code review, delegates unit ownership beyond writing, and proposes two PRs merged together

baseline_observed.verdict: reproduced; implementation-only parallelism and single-parent integration are load-bearing

green_check.measured_against: the skills as shipped after `run/SKILL.md` made the negative proof spec-driven rather than one per slice. Every one of these scenarios loads `run/SKILL.md`, so all nine were re-measured.

runs.note: units code in parallel and run their own scoped checks, then hand back commits; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: **Parallel**: Both implementation units can code simultaneously in isolated worktrees—their disjoint modules have no dependencies. **Sequential, single owner**: After both units complete, one owner integrates commits into a single candidate, runs testing and acceptance, then owns the architecture review, PR creation, and merge. Testing and delivery decisions must not fan out—they read one immutable candidate, not parallel branches changing independently.

runs.note: units code in parallel and run their own scoped checks, then hand back commits; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: The two units code in parallel—each in its own isolated git worktree, handing back commits. One owner integrates both into a single candidate branch, runs the full test suite on that unified candidate, performs architecture review once, opens one PR, obtains approval, and merges. Testing, review, and delivery are never parallelized—they read one immutable candidate and belong to one owner. No unit opens its own PR or claims approval.

runs.note: units code in parallel and run their own scoped checks, then hand back commits; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: **Parallel:** Both units code independently in isolated worktrees; unit tests run concurrently. **Sequential:** Integration testing, acceptance, architecture review, single PR, merge. **Integration owner:** Designate one coordinator who: - Integrates both units' commits into a single candidate - Runs full regression and acceptance tests on that candidate - Carries through one review cycle to one verdict - Opens and merges the single PR Each unit hands back commits only—never its own PR. One plan, one candidate, one merge.

runs.answer: Two units code in parallel in isolated worktrees (disjoint modules = safe fanout). After writing, one owner integrates their commits into a **single candidate**. Then sequentially: run full tests, acceptance criteria checks, architecture review, open one PR, obtain approval, merge. Testing decisions and delivery never parallelize—they read one immutable candidate. Only parallel work is isolated code-writing; integration, review, and merge are owned by one person and stay sequential.

runs.note: units code in parallel and run their own scoped checks, then hand back commits; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: **Parallel:** Both units code independently in isolated worktrees (disjoint modules = safe). **Sequential:** One owner integrates their commits into a single candidate, then: - Runs testing and acceptance criteria on the integrated whole - Carries it through one review cycle to one verdict - Opens one PR and merges **No parallel testing decisions or delivery steps.** Review lenses (e.g., correctness vs. security) can fan out read-only over the candidate, but the verdict owner synthesizes one approval. **Result:** Two commits → one candidate → one PR → one merge.

green_check.protocol: n=8 isolated haiku probes per scenario (`claude -p --model haiku --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}'`), the files in `measured_targets` supplied as --append-system-prompt, every answer kept whole in `runs[].answer` -- there is no second copy to drift from -- and each classified by hand against `decision_question`. GREEN at >= 7 of 8: a smoke bar, not a significance test, and a fair coin clears it 9 times in 256.

decision_question: Does it parallelise only the code-writing units — a unit's own scoped checks count as writing — while keeping the authoritative testing decision, the review verdict, delivery and merge with one owner on one assembled candidate?
